synoptic.summary: The trough that brought Friday's breezy flow from 300°–360° is departing south and high pressure builds in from Saturday, giving dry, stable, mostly clear weather through at least Monday. Saturday follows the normal diurnal cycle with very light flow aloft (under 6 kt up to 5,500 ft above landing). From Sunday the GFS turns the flow aloft to 160°–220° (up to 12–14 kt at 2,000–3,700 ft above landing early Sunday) and the launch forecasts stay at 150°–180° all day Sunday and Monday — no afternoon switch to 320°–360°, a departure from the usual pattern that favors POM South and shuts POM North and Cherry. No convection (thunder 0%, precipitation ≤1%). Valley inversions and haze are expected to build by Sunday–Monday.
synoptic.afd_excerpt: High pressure will spread across the area throughout the day on Saturday, bringing dry and stable conditions areawide. With warming temperatures overhead, anticipate a gradual warming trend through the weekend alongside largely clear skies.

pressure.significance: Salt Lake airport sea-level pressure 1025.3 mb at 16:54 Fri, up from 1022.2 mb 19 h earlier as the high builds behind the departing trough. Stable, light-gradient pattern — favorable, especially mornings.

observations.summary: Friday late afternoon (16:15–17:15 local) the valley stations still show the departing trough's flow from 290°–360° at 7–16 kt, gusting to 19 kt at Spanish Fork. These evening readings say little about Saturday morning, when the forecast has light drainage from ~140°. Point of the Mountain and Draper returned no data; South Valley Regional's newest report is from 15:15 (about 2 h old at fetch).
